result.title: AV-FLARE: Feature-Level Reliability Estimation for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
result.comment: Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 2027 IEEE Symposium Series on Computational Intelligence (IEEE SSCI 2027)
result.summary: Multimodal emotion recognition (MMER) systems typically rely on learned feature representations and attention mechanisms that implicitly weight information across time and modalities. However, these mechanisms do not explicitly incorporate input reliability, despite the presence of noise in audio, occlusions in visual data, and the sparse and event-driven nature of affective cues. We propose AV-FLARE, a framework that explicitly estimates fine-grained reliability scores across both temporal and feature dimensions prior to temporal modeling and uses them to modulate feature representations. Reliability is computed using two complementary components: (i) a supervised network trained jointly with the classification objective, and (ii) an unsupervised Gaussian Mixture Model that models global feature distributions. These signals are combined to provide both task-driven and distribution-aware reliability estimates. To integrate modalities, we introduce a hierarchical cross-modal attention mechanism in which textual features are used to guide audio-visual fusion as a semantic reference modality. Experiments on the IEMOCAP dataset show that AV-FLARE improves over a no-reliability baseline, achieving 90.81\% accuracy and 81.69\% F1-score, corresponding to gains of +4.41% and +8.56%, respectively. These results suggest that incorporating explicit input reliability estimation may improve robustness in multimodal emotion recognition under the evaluated setting.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AV-FLARE，在时序建模前从时间与特征两个维度显式估计细粒度可靠性分数并据此调制特征表示，可靠性由与分类任务联合训练的监督网络和无监督 GMM 两部分构成，再以文本为语义参考引导音视频分层跨模态注意力融合，在 IEMOCAP 上取得提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先估计模态与特征可靠性再加权调制」的做法，可供核查是否能迁移为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与噪声门控；但论文任务是情感识别而非生成式推理，未涉及 latent 推理状态、视觉旁路或停止决策，联系仅停留在输入筛选层面。
